title: Structure of a real project
summary: Split by responsibility: routers, services, repositories, schemas, models and configuration with pydantic-settings.

sections.definition: Split by responsibility: routers (HTTP), services (business rules), repositories (data access), schemas (Pydantic), models (tables) and configuration with pydantic-settings. APIRouter modularizes the routes and lifespan handles startup and shutdown (the on_event events are deprecated).
sections.analogy: In a restaurant, the waiter (router) takes the order, the chef (service) decides how to prepare it and the storekeeper (repository) brings the ingredients. The waiter doesn't cook and the chef doesn't wait tables.
sections.problem: With everything in main.py, business logic ends up mixed with HTTP and SQL: it cannot be tested without starting the API nor reused from a script or a worker.
sections.code:example:
tienda-api/
├── pyproject.toml
├── uv.lock
├── .env                    # nunca al repo
├── alembic.ini
├── migrations/
├── app/
│   ├── main.py             # crea FastAPI, lifespan, incluye routers
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── config.py       # Settings
│   │   └── security.py     # hash y JWT
│   ├── db.py               # engine y get_session
│   ├── deps.py             # SessionDep, ClienteActual
│   ├── pedidos/
│   │   ├── router.py
│   │   ├── schemas.py
│   │   ├── models.py
│   │   ├── service.py
│   │   └── repository.py
│   └── productos/ ...
└── tests/
# app/core/config.py
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict

class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env")
    database_url: str
    secret_key: str
    token_minutos: int = 30
    cors_origins: list[str] = ["http://localhost:4200"]

settings = Settings()

# app/pedidos/router.py
router = APIRouter(prefix="/pedidos", tags=["pedidos"])

@router.post("", status_code=201)
def crear(datos: PedidoCrear, cliente: ClienteActual, session: SessionDep) -> PedidoPublico:
    return PedidoService(session).crear(datos, cliente)

# app/main.py
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # arranque: conexiones, cargar modelos de IA, etc.
    yield
    # apagado: liberar recursos

app = FastAPI(title="Tienda API", lifespan=lifespan)
app.include_router(pedidos.router)
app.include_router(productos.router)
sections.bad:
@app.post("/pedidos")
def crear(datos: dict):
    con = psycopg.connect("postgres://admin:1234@...")
    total = sum(i["precio"] * i["cantidad"] for i in datos["items"])
    if total > 1_000_000: ...
    con.execute(f"INSERT INTO pedido ...")

Credentials in the code, no validation, rules and SQL in the handler.
sections.good:
@router.post("", status_code=201)
def crear(datos: PedidoCrear, servicio: PedidoServiceDep) -> PedidoPublico:
    return servicio.crear(datos)

The router only translates HTTP; the service holds the rule and is tested on its own.
sections.bridge:typescript: It is the organization by features you already use on the frontend: each folder with its router (like the feature's routes), its services and its models. Settings ≈ a per-environment configuration file or import.meta.env, but it is read from environment variables at runtime, not at build time.
sections.interview: I organize by features, and within each one I separate router, schemas, models, service and, if needed, repository. The router only handles HTTP; the service has the business rules and knows nothing about HTTP; the repository encapsulates the queries. Configuration comes from environment variables with pydantic-settings, common dependencies live in a deps module, and I use lifespan for startup and shutdown. I adjust the number of layers to the size of the project.
sections.myths:
• Overengineering: a repository for a three-table CRUD may be overkill. Start simple.
  • Committing the .env with secrets.
  • Using @app.on_event("startup"): it is deprecated, use lifespan.
  • Circular imports between modules of different features.
